notes: FROZEN — no phases. GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.78 DOES raise blocking dialogs that name no tool call: the first-use workspace-trust modal ('Do you trust the files in this folder?'), MCP OAuth and headers-refresh prompts for a configured server, server-driven or agent-initiated MCP elicitation (ElicitationRequestedData documents elicitationSource as 'MCP server name, or absent for agent-initiated' and does NOT require toolCallId), and the product's own auto_mode_switch / session_limits_exhausted reviews. The sandbox and network-access confirmations also exist but are FIELDS on a tool-carrying permission request (requestSandboxBypass on PermissionRequestUrl / PermissionRequestRead; the constant 'outside the sandbox, bypassing its protections.'), so they belong to tool-gate-permission-prompt / permission-gate-non-mutating-tool and substituting one is what this row forbids. So agent_supports is yes. NONE OF IT IS OBSERVABLE, and copilot states why in its own shipped schema. schemas/session-events.schema.json gives 64 of its 148 typed event definitions an `ephemeral` property declared as {"const": true, "description": "Always true for events that are transient and not persisted to the session event log on disk."} — and that set contains elicitation.requested/completed, user_input.requested/completed, exit_plan_mode.requested/completed, auto_mode_switch.requested/completed, session_limits_exhausted.requested/completed, mcp.oauth_required/completed, mcp.headers_refresh_required/completed, sampling.requested/completed and session.managed_settings_enforced/resolved. Of the request families only permission.requested/permission.completed (and external_tool.requested) are persisted, and a permission request carries a toolCallId by construction. app.js corroborates at the emitter: PendingRequests is constructed as (emitEphemeral, emit, sessionId) and only requestPermissionPrompt and requestExternalToolTracked take the persisted branch, while emitInternal's ephemeral branch skips sessionRecordEventJson entirely. THE WORKSPACE-TRUST TRIGGER IS BLOCKED HARDER STILL: it is a React overlay with no emit of any kind, and it fires BEFORE the input box — irrlicht's own copilot driver documents that it 'blocks the input box entirely' and that seeding trustedFolders into config.json is not sufficient (verified 1.0.77). At that moment copilot has created session-state/<id>/ with only workspace.yaml and has written no events.jsonl, so no real session row exists; the daemon holds only the transient proc-<PID> presession, born ready. The row's ready → working → waiting arc has no session to happen on. NO HOOK CARRIES IT EITHER. Copilot fires its notification hook from six sites in app.js, and the only two blocked-on-user types are permission_prompt and elicitation_dialog — the system-notification path passes a kind enum of agent_completed | agent_idle | new_inbox_message | shell_completed | shell_detached_completed | instruction_discovered | unclassified, none a dialog, with the two agent_* kinds excluded from firing at all. That matches irrlicht's receiver, which recognises exactly those two types. The one family that does reach the daemon, elicitation_dialog, still cannot satisfy this row: handleNotificationHook is DISPATCH ONLY (session.HookSignal has no Notification row, so no hold is taken and the session reads working, not waiting) — a deliberate, documented decision, because copilot emits nothing at all when a prompt is denied (verified live on 1.0.78: no Stop, no postToolUse, no postToolUseFailure, no errorOccurred in 42 s) so an unreleasable hold would pin the session to the 12-hour ceiling — and, decisively, elicitation.completed is itself ephemeral:const true and fires no notification, so the RELEASE edge this row also asserts has no trace on any channel. LADDER: with no permission.requested on disk and no hook hold, none of the five waiting rules in state_classifier.go is reachable — permission_prompt has no signal, transcript_permission_prompt needs TranscriptPermissionPending, user_blocking_tool and open_tool_stalled both need an OPEN tool call which this row's premise excludes by definition, and idle_prompt is unset. The session reads working (or ready, if the tail already looks turn-done) for the whole time the modal blocks. WHY NO PHASES ARE AUTHORED (the vacuous-pass rule): absence of a waiting episode and inability to raise the dialog would produce identical events.jsonl, and on 1.0.78 both are the expected output. Worse, copilot CAN reach waiting by two other routes — the transcript-tier permission rule (2-19) and the trailing-question path (2-17) — so ANY waiting a recording of this row showed would by construction NOT be the tool-less dialog. A spec with phases here would be an invitation to read a coincidence as a pass. ONE UNVERIFIED HOLE, marked rather than dismissed: app.js exposes a native host effect `fire_notification_hook` through which the embedded Rust core can request a notification of an ARBITRARY type, so the six-call-site census bounds only the JavaScript half. A `strings -n 6` scan of the 159 MB Node SEA produced 382,525 lines of Node internals and zero hits for notificationType / permission_prompt / elicitation_dialog / idle_prompt — the core's string table is not readable that way, so the scan could not look rather than looked and found nothing. If the core does fire a notification for the trust or auto-mode dialog, the ENTRY edge becomes hook-reachable; the release edge still would not be. RE-ASSESS WHEN: copilot persists elicitation.requested/completed or fires a completion notification; or copilot fires the notification hook for a genuinely tool-less dialog together with a paired release; or the adapter gains a Source over the live event stream rather than the persisted log. The elicitation seam is the tractable one — the workspace-trust one is not, because it is pre-session.
